subject.title: [Feature]: Automatic Output Sanitization for Sensitive Data

question: Should OpenClaw add automatic sensitive-value sanitization to final/user-visible outputs in core, or keep that behavior as an opt-in plugin/hook policy?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but choosing the sanitizer boundary changes user-visible output semantics, security expectations, false-positive behavior, and likely config defaults.

options.title: Approve narrow core sanitizer
options.body: Add an opt-in or explicitly scoped core final-output sanitizer using existing redaction helpers, with schema/docs/tests and clear false-positive/reporting behavior.

options.title: Use plugin-first output filtering
options.body: Document reply_payload_sending/message_sending as the supported sanitizer seam and route concrete sanitizer packages through plugin or ClawHub distribution.

options.title: Keep current boundary
options.body: Declare log, transcript, tool-payload, diagnostic, and internal-scaffolding cleanup as the supported core redaction boundary and narrow or close this request later.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow core sanitizer
recommendation.body: Add an opt-in or explicitly scoped core final-output sanitizer using existing redaction helpers, with schema/docs/tests and clear false-positive/reporting behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the member backlog comment on the related sensitive-data umbrella and are the clearest available security/product routing signal from the discussion.
